Fountain of Living Waters
FOWN-tin uv LIV-ing WAW-turz
phrase (biblical title of God)
From Jeremiah 2:13, where the LORD names Himself “the fountain of living waters”; fulfilled in Christ's words at the well (John 4:10-14) and the feast (John 7:37-39). “Living waters” means fresh, running, spring water.

📖 Biblical Definition

The fountain of living waters is a title of the LORD Himself, and of Christ who freely gives the Spirit—the soul's one true and inexhaustible satisfaction. In Jeremiah the LORD mourns that His people have forsaken Him, “the fountain of living waters,” for broken cisterns. A fountain of living waters is no stagnant pool but a spring of fresh, running water, ever flowing, never failing, freely available to all who come. Such is God to His people. The figure flowers fully in the Gospel of John. To the woman at the well Christ says, “If thou knewest the gift of God… thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water,” and again, “the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.” At the feast He cries, “If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink”—and John explains, “this spake he of the Spirit.” Here is the whole gospel in a figure: the thirsty soul, parched and weary of broken cisterns, is bidden to come to Christ and drink. The water He gives is the Spirit, who springs up within unto everlasting life. The fountain costs the comer nothing, for Christ has paid all; it never runs dry, for it is God Himself; and it alone can satisfy, for the soul was made for Him.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A title of the LORD, and of Christ who gives the Spirit—the fresh, freely flowing spring that alone satisfies the thirsty soul.

FOUNTAIN OF LIVING WATERS, phrase (biblical title of God). From Jeremiah 2:13; “living waters” meaning fresh, running spring water, here a title of God Himself.

The inexhaustible spring of all satisfaction, contrasted with the broken cisterns of idols.

Fulfilled in Christ, who gives living water that springs up into everlasting life.

As recorded in Scripture: “Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God… thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water” (John 4:10).

By extension, the gift of the Holy Spirit, freely poured out on all who come to Christ and drink.

📖 Key Scripture

Jer 2:13 — "For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water."

Joh 4:14 — "But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life."

Joh 7:37 — "In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink."

Rev 22:17 — "And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition, though the soul's thirst is misdirected wherever the world is offered as the satisfaction only God can give.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The figure is not the object of ideological dispute, but the truth it carries cuts against the whole spirit of an age that bids the thirsty soul drink at every cistern but the true Fountain. Wealth, pleasure, and the endless pursuit of self are pressed as the springs of satisfaction, when they are the very broken cisterns Jeremiah named.

The principle to recover is that God alone satisfies. The soul was made for Him and thirsts until it drinks of Him; no creature can fill the cistern He alone was made to fill. The remedy is the free offer of the gospel: “let him that is athirst come… and take the water of life freely.” Christ stands at the feast still crying, “If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.” The fountain is open, full, and free; the only condition is to come thirsty.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The figure runs from Jeremiah's title of God to Christ's gift of the Spirit and the open invitation of Revelation.

expand to see more

“Living waters” means fresh, running spring water as opposed to stored or stagnant.

Jeremiah 2:13 names the LORD Himself as that fountain, forsaken for broken cisterns.

John 4 has Christ offering living water that springs up into everlasting life.

John 7:37-39 identifies the living water with the gift of the Holy Spirit.

Revelation 22:17 issues the final invitation to take the water of life freely.

Usage

"The phrase names God and Christ as the soul's only true and lasting satisfaction."

"Preachers set the fountain against broken cisterns to press the free offer of the gospel."

"Believers return to it when parched, drinking afresh of Christ and His Spirit."
